neutral_facts.value: The accused raped a seven-year-old girl. The victim was proceeding towards Haar from her home when the accused met her and took her near the river Parvati. He removed her undergarment, made her sit on his lap, and discharged on her private parts and stomach. The victim shouted, and her mother arrived at the scene. The accused fled. The victim narrated the incident to her mother, leading to the lodging of an FIR. The investigating agency examined witnesses, seized the accused's clothes, and sent items for forensic examination. The trial court convicted the accused under s. 376(2)(f) rw s. 511 and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for five years. The High Court converted the offence to one under s. 354 and reduced the sentence to the period already undergone.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that in cases of rape or attempted rape, there cannot be a compromise or settlement as it would be against the honour of the victim, which is sacrosanct. The Court emphasized that the appellate court must reappreciate the evidence and not dismiss appeals summarily without examining the evidence.

quotes.text: In a case of rape or attempt of rape, the conception of compromise under no circumstances can really be thought of. These are crimes against the body of a woman which is her own temple. These are offences which suffocate the breath of life and sully the reputation.
